registration.stage: Stage 4: value model and engineering mechanism validation

research_scope.primary_question: Do the registered value-model terms and true-state repair mechanism produce the intended engineering-level effects when candidate identities, random seeds, state trajectories, and the external evaluator are held fixed?
research_scope.interpretation_boundary: This stage validates controlled-simulation mechanisms and engineering-shaped transfer. It does not establish field deployment effectiveness or superiority over a commercial operational system.
research_scope.solver_boundary: The mechanism-isolation arms use the same bounded-search backend and a shared complete-model candidate pool. External engineering arms include Greedy and External-Auction under the same shared pool. Solver superiority is not an endpoint of this stage.

registered_hypotheses.name: compatibility
registered_hypotheses.test: CA-HMCD should improve the unified external objective and independent service score relative to No-Compatibility in engineering-shaped scenarios.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: A module is treated as supported only when the prespecified paired interval and Holm-adjusted comparison support the direction; otherwise the result is reported as unsupported or context-dependent.

registered_hypotheses.name: complementarity
registered_hypotheses.test: The CA-HMCD minus No-Synergy difference should be near zero at synergy scale 0 and increase with the registered complementarity scale in the controlled sweep.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: The intended claim is context-dependent complementarity, not universal aggregate superiority.

registered_hypotheses.name: redundancy
registered_hypotheses.test: Under the registered redundancy-stress scenario, CA-HMCD should reduce same-type pair ratio, capability overlap, and marginal-gain waste relative to No-Redundancy without materially sacrificing service.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: If the diagnostics do not move, the redundancy mechanism is not claimed as empirically validated.

registered_hypotheses.name: stability
registered_hypotheses.test: Relative to No-Stability, CA-HMCD should reduce allocation switching as volatility increases, while the objective/service trade-off is reported explicitly.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: No claim is made that stability improves every instantaneous service metric.

registered_hypotheses.name: true_state_repair
registered_hypotheses.test: Under perception disturbance, RepairOn should improve final feasibility and service relative to the identical RepairOff trajectory.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: Repair is a feasibility safeguard; objective restoration is not required for support.

registered_hypotheses.name: engineering_transfer
registered_hypotheses.test: Across the five engineering-shaped scenarios, CA-HMCD should retain feasible allocations and provide a scenario-qualified service/coverage profile relative to Greedy and External-Auction.
registered_hypotheses.claim_boundary: HiGHS is not re-ranked in this stage and no universal superiority claim is registered.

statistical_plan.paired_difference: CA-HMCD-family arm minus comparator arm on the same seed and stratum
statistical_plan.interval: 95% BCa bootstrap interval for mean paired difference, deterministic seed derived from family and endpoint
statistical_plan.bounded_intervals: Wilson score intervals for episode-level feasibility, raw feasibility, repair rate, same-type pair ratio, capability overlap, and marginal-gain waste
statistical_plan.multiple_comparison: Holm step-down separately within every registered family listed in holm_families.csv

decision_rules.repair_supported: At least one non-zero noise level has a positive paired 95% BCa lower bound for final feasibility and Holm-adjusted P < 0.05, with the RepairOn final feasibility rate not below 0.95.
decision_rules.stability_supported: At least three non-zero volatility levels show a negative CA-HMCD minus No-Stability switch-count difference with the prespecified interval and Holm-adjusted P < 0.05.
decision_rules.redundancy_supported: At least two of the three independent redundancy diagnostics show a negative CA-HMCD minus No-Redundancy difference with the prespecified interval and Holm-adjusted P < 0.05, while service loss is no more than 0.02 in absolute mean.
decision_rules.complementarity_supported: Scale 0 is an identity control and the scale-2 paired objective difference is positive with the prespecified interval and Holm-adjusted P < 0.05; monotonicity is summarized descriptively and does not override the paired test.
decision_rules.engineering_transfer_supported: All five scenarios remain feasible, and CA-HMCD has a positive service-score or coverage difference against at least one external baseline in at least three scenarios after the registered Holm family correction.

reproducibility.resume_policy: Existing shards are reused only when unit identity, protocol fingerprint, runner version, and current code hashes match exactly.
reproducibility.failure_policy: A failed unit is recorded and stops formal completion; no automatic retry is performed.
reproducibility.data_policy: All outputs remain local. No raw data or results are uploaded to external services.
